parameters.content:
## Salon Booking Bot — core (Phase 2)
CP0 Echo: Webhook → Normalize (adapter boundary; sender_key = "{channel}:{id}") → Build Reply → Respond.
CP1 Front gate: Load Config (MOCK) → Validate Payload → Reject 400.
CP2 State: Load / Merge / Save State (Airtable conversations, keyed by sender_key; turn_count).
CP3 Guards: Check Bot Guards (kill-switch + max-turns) run BEFORE the LLM → Handoff Reply (transient).
CP3 LLM intent: Build LLM Request ({today} + derived schema) → Extract Intent (HTTP → Anthropic; error → LLM Unavailable Reply 503) → Validate Intent (ajv-standalone from committed schema) → Confidence & Intent Gate → Mark Handoff (stage=handoff) / Save State.
Three handoff classes stay distinct: guard-trip (200, transient) · infra-unavailable (503) · intent-handoff (200, writes stage=handoff).
Error branches visible (400 / 503). Zernio swaps in at Normalize (Phase 4).

parameters.content:
## Guards — before the LLM (0 cost)
**Check Bot Guards** runs before any LLM call:
- `killSwitch` ON **or** `turn_count ≥ maxTurns` → **Handoff Reply** (200) — no LLM, no Save State (a trip is not a turn).
- else → **Save State** (`turn_count +1`) → normal flow.
Config comes from `Load Config` (`bot.killSwitch`, `bot.maxTurnsPerConversation`).

⚠️ Conscious gap (not a bug): while `stage = handoff` the bot re-sends the handoff
template on every message. The silent-lock (**Check Handoff Lock**) lands in **CP6**.

Extract Intent — ERROR output = LLM INFRA FAILURE
(timeout / 5xx / rate-limit / quota).
→ "LLM Unavailable Reply": 503 + error:"llm_unavailable",
   polite customer reply kept. DISTINCT from the
   conversational handoff (200, "Handoff Reply").
CP5: Telegram owner-alert attaches to this node.

⚠ A 5xx tells the caller to RETRY. Before Phase 4
(Zernio calls this webhook and may retry on a 503) the
status-code policy is reviewed; Phase-3 idempotency
(processed_messages) covers those repeats.
Note: all Respond nodes are the Phase-2 transport layer;
in Phase 4 the reply is sent via the Zernio send API and
this webhook response becomes an ACK (adapter boundary, node 28).

## CP4 — Slot-filling (multi-turn booking)
Route Intent: book → collect · else → passthrough (stored slots carried UNCHANGED — a mid-booking FAQ never wipes them).
Merge Slots: DETERMINISTIC accumulate (this turn's LLM slots ∪ stored) — not the LLM.
Slot Gate: required {service, date, time} complete? → stage new→collecting→ready + next_ask (service|datetime).
Build LLM Request is STAGE-AWARE: on 'collecting' it feeds the LLM the booking-in-progress context, so a bare "tomorrow 3pm" is read as slots.
Build Reply: ready→confirm · collecting→ask(next_ask) · handoff→template.
Availability check + booking WRITE = Phase 3.

## CP6 — Handoff silent-lock + returning greeting

**Check Handoff Lock** (runs BEFORE the LLM): if the thread is already `stage='handoff'` (a human took over via `Mark Handoff`), short-circuit → **Handoff Lock Reply** (200, `locked:true`). No LLM cost · no `Save State` (turn_count frozen) · the bot never talks over the human.

Only intent-handoff writes `stage='handoff'`; a guard-trip writes no state → it never locks. Release = owner clears `stage` in Airtable (manual, mock).

**Returning greeting** (in `Build Reply Payload`): `found` + session-gap (`now − last_updated_prev > bot.sessionGapMinutes`, both UTC) → 'Welcome back!' on the opening reply only, never mid-conversation.

**Phase 5:** owner-alert (Telegram) also hooks `Handoff Lock Reply` → owner is pinged on a new message to an already-locked thread.

## Phase 3 · CP1 — Availability check (read-only)

When slots are complete (`stage='ready'`) the bot checks the REAL Google Calendar BEFORE confirming — no write yet (that is CP2).

`Availability Gate` (ready?) → `Build FreeBusy Query` → `Get Calendar Busy` (**freeBusy**, service-account, 15s timeout) → `Compute Availability` (working hours − busy; fits duration? + alternatives; **fail-loud on freeBusy `errors`**).

available → `stage='confirming'` + confirm ask · busy → alternatives · closed/past → re-ask. GCal down / freeBusy-error → **`Calendar Unavailable Reply`** (503 `calendar_unavailable`). Confirmed “yes” → write = **CP2**.

parameters.content:
## CP2b — Write-then-verify (no-double-book)
Book Appointment → **Verify Slot** (events.list over booked window) → **Check Race** (drop cancelled/transparent; any OTHER overlap = lost race) → **Race Gate**.

- **clean**: Cancel Our Event OK → handoff (`slotJustTaken`)
- **orphan**: delete FAILED → keep `gcal_event_id` for owner cleanup → handoff
- **verify read down**: keep event, **200** (never 503→retry double-book), handoff (`bookingNeedsConfirm`)
- **mirror fail**: Write Appointment error → **Build Mirror-Failed State** (`mirror_failed` flag, still "booked" — GCal is authoritative)

Always delete **OUR** `gcal_event_id`, never a pre-existing event. Insert→Verify is a direct edge (no slow node) to keep the read-after-write window tight.

**LIMITS (honest — no atomic lock; see ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS §5):**
- Symmetric TOCTOU (two NEW writers) → both yield → slot empty (safe, not "exactly one").
- Assumes GCal read-your-writes; if both verifies miss each other → double-book. Narrowed, not closed.
- Real fix = DB `UNIQUE(date,time)` (deferred: Postgres = T1→T2 tier bump). Idempotency = CP2c.

## CP2c-i — Idempotency front-gate (message-ID dedupe)
Normalize (+`message_id`, REQUIRED in Validate Payload → 400 if missing) → **Check Processed** (search `processed_messages`) → **Dedupe Gate** (re-attach payload + `_duplicate`) → **Is Duplicate**.
- duplicate → **Idempotent Replay** (200 `duplicate_ignored`, no LLM / no write)
- new → Load State (normal flow)

**Record Processed** writes the id AFTER `Save State` success (parallel terminal branch) → a transient-failure retry is NOT blocked (only successfully-processed messages are recorded). Check Processed down → **503 state_unavailable** (never assume 'not duplicate'). Booking-layer insert-idempotency = CP2c-ii.

## CP2c-ii — booking-layer insert-idempotency
**Deterministic event id** = hex(`sender_key|date|time|service`) set in Build Event Request → Book Appointment sends it as the event `id`. A duplicate insert (retry / lost response) → **409**.

Book Appointment error → **Get For Reconcile** (GET by that id):
- found & `status != cancelled` → **Reconcile Gate** true → Verify Slot (idempotent — no 2nd event)
- found & cancelled (tombstone) → **Build Reconcile-Handoff State** → handoff
- GET fails / 404 (never created) → Calendar Unavailable Reply **503** (retry safe)

**Never 503 before the GET reconcile.** Downstream reads `Build Event Request.booking.eventId` (exists on the 409 path). Write Appointment is upsert-on-gcal_event_id (mirror idempotent).

## CP3 — Cancel (customer cancels their OWN booking)
Route Intent `cancel` → **Find Booking** (Airtable appointments by **sender_key + status=booked** → IDOR-safe) → **Cancel Lookup** (next-upcoming) → **Cancel Route**:
- **confirm** → Build Cancel-Confirm State (`cancel_confirming`, names the appt) → next "yes" → **execute** (3b: delete the EXACT gcal_event_id, never guessed → Airtable cancelled)
- **none** → No-Booking · **needs_human** → blank gcal_event_id (old data) → handoff · **cutoff** → within `cancellationCutoffHours` → handoff

Identity = channel-auth `sender_key`, NEVER a customer-supplied booking id (IDOR structurally impossible). Widget sessionId = session-token strength; hardened Phase 5/6 (ARCH-DEC).

parameters.content:
## Cancel-confirm lifecycle — fail-closed
A "yes" here DELETES a real calendar event, so every gate defaults to
"do nothing / booking stands". Three look-alike gates — don't confuse them:

- **Confirm Router** — `stage === 'cancel_confirming'`? Is this message landing on a
  thread that is awaiting a cancel confirmation at all. (in vs. normal routing)
- **Confirm Fresh?** — is that confirmation still inside its 1-turn TTL?
- **Confirm Live?** — right before the DELETE, does the booking still exist and still
  bind to the same target?

**TTL — why `confirm_turn`.** On the confirm prompt we stamp `confirm_turn` = the turn
the "yes" must land on. Confirm Fresh? passes ONLY when `turn_count === confirm_turn`.
A "yes" that arrives a turn later (or a replayed/stale message) → abort, never delete.

**Fail-CLOSED — validate BEFORE you coerce.** Confirm Fresh? type-checks first
(`turn_count` positive safe-int; `confirm_turn` canonical `/^[1-9][0-9]*$/` string), THEN
compares as strings. Never `Number()` first: `Number(null)===0` / `Number('')===0` — a
legacy row with no/0 `confirm_turn` would falsely read as "turn 0 == turn 0" and delete.
null / '' / 0 / type-mismatch all → Build Cancel-Aborted State (booking stands).

**Pre-delete re-read — what it does & does NOT do.** Re-read Cancel State → Verify
Confirm Live → Confirm Live? re-reads the conversation row IMMEDIATELY before the DELETE,
so a state changed since the confirm (already consumed / rebound) stops the delete. This
is NOT an atomic lock — it narrows the race from the whole run to two nodes; a tight
concurrent race remains. Full fix = per-sender serialization → **Phase 5**.

**Abort Cancel?** — `stage===cancel_confirming` AND `intent!=='confirm'`: they said
something other than "yes" while awaiting confirmation → drop the pending cancel.

conditions.leftValue: ={{ (() => { const tc = $json.state.turn_count; const ct = $json.state.confirm_turn; if (typeof tc !== 'number' || !Number.isSafeInteger(tc) || tc <= 0) return false; if (typeof ct !== 'string' || !/^[1-9][0-9]*$/.test(ct)) return false; return String(tc) === ct; })() }}

parameters.content:
## Verify Zernio Signature (CRT #3)
Inbound Zernio WhatsApp is HMAC-SHA256 signed (X-Zernio-Signature = lowercase hex of the RAW body). **Is Zernio Inbound?** routes nested Zernio payloads → **Compute Body HMAC** (binary raw body + crypto credential) → **Signature Valid?** → **Reject Unsigned Request** (403) if missing/wrong. Widget skips this (no shared secret; Phase-5 rate-limit/Turnstile). The ONLY path to a whatsapp: sender_key is a valid signature here.

## Outbound convergence (CP4b)
Every reply branch tags _outbound_* (VERBATIM body + status) -> Finalize Outbound -> Channel Switch:
- widget -> Send Reply (widget): synchronous body+status, bit-identical to before.
- whatsapp -> (CP4b-2) ACK 200 first, then Zernio send.

_outbound_should_send rule: send only if the customer must learn something they don't already know (duplicate/handoff-lock = already knows -> no send). Reject Unsigned Request stays SEPARATE.

**whatsapp ACK is intentionally ALWAYS 200** (transport ACK to Zernio's delivery layer, NOT the customer) — do NOT couple it to `_outbound_status`; a 5xx here would trigger a provider retry storm. On whatsapp the infra-unavailable distinctness (handoff.md's 5xx) lives in the `error`/`_outbound_*` state fields + the distinct Unavailable node, not the HTTP status (which is the widget/sync semantics). `_outbound_owner_flag` on a failed send is surfaced by the owner-alert = Phase 5.

parameters.content:
## Spend-cap (CP5b-2)
Read the month's accumulated LLM cost (`bot_metrics`) BEFORE the LLM. Under `bot.llmCostCapUsd` -> proceed; over -> deterministic handoff reply (200, no state write) + owner alert. After a successful call `Record LLM Spend` adds tokens x config price. **Fail-OPEN**: a meter read/write error still lets the LLM run, but `Build Spend-Meter Alert` warns the owner (K-SPEND).

## Global dry-run (CP5b-3, subset B)
`bot.dryRun=true` blocks the two real-world writes: the new-booking **GCal event insert** (`Live Booking?` -> dry state, no event) and the **whatsapp send** (`Live Send?` -> NoOp). Fail-safe OR with the other brakes. Reschedule/cancel need a real booking, which dry-run prevents creating, so gating new-booking + sends neutralizes real writes. Reminder sends have their own `whatsappSendDisabled` brake. Default **false** (live).

## Signature + adapter hardening (CP5d)
**Verify Signature**: constant-time HMAC compare (plain-JS XOR, no crypto — spike-verified unavailable). Hygiene, not a claimed timing-attack barrier.
**Normalize graceful reject**: no more throw->bare 500. whatsapp drift (authentic, signature-verified) -> 422 + owner-alert `normalize_drift` (independent signal in Zernio's log too); widget bad-shape -> 400, NO alert (unauth endpoint -> alert-channel DoS guard).
